details.label: Discussion
details.text: Latest mesoanalysis places the western flank of a broadly bowing MCS in progress over southeast IN into southwest OH in close proximity to a warm front slowly advancing east through portions of northern and eastern KY. There, earlier VWP data from KILN and current objective analysis indicate a slight enhancement of low-level shear, which coincides with a favorable shear-cold pool balance along the leading edge of the convective system. As such, the potential exists for brief tornadoes, particularly where the MCS intersects the warm front. Otherwise, the setup appears favorable for more concentrated damaging wind potential with gusts up to 70-80 mph. The watch may need to be locally extended across a greater portion of eastern Kentucky

details.label: Discussion
details.text: A west-to-east-oriented band of thunderstorms has recently intensified across portions of east-central IL into west-central IN, to the north of an outflow boundary from earlier convection. The 18Z ILX sounding is likely representative of the inflow environment with steep mid-level lapse rates and a moist boundary layer yielding MLCAPE of 2000-2500 J/kg. The current storms might still be slightly elevated atop a shallow surface inversion. However, a continued storm motion toward the more unstable environment should support a transition to surface-based updrafts with an increasing threat for damaging wind gusts as the attending cold pool matures. Prior to that, isolated occurrences of severe hail are possible. The severe threat is expected to largely spread southeast into the watch area over the next hour, so an additional watch to the west in IL is not currently anticipated. However, the current watch may need to be locally extended into southwest IN

details.label: Discussion
details.text: Recent visible satellite imagery depicts agitated cumulus developing along the Black Hills in western South Dakota. Widely scattered thunderstorm development is likely across this region and within a weak surface confluence zone noted just west of the ND/SD/MT border. The 18z UNR observed sounding sampled 2000 J/kg MLCAPE and steep mid-level lapse rates of 8-9 C/km, with further destabilization expected through the afternoon (MLCAPE forecast to exceed 3000 J/kg by peak heating). Enhanced westerly flow aloft is also yielding elongated, relatively linear hodographs and 40-50 kts of effective shear, which will support splitting supercells. Ample buoyancy within the hail growth zone, steep mid-level lapse rates, and a favorable storm mode will promote a threat for large to very large hail of 2-3+ inches in diameter. Isolated giant hail (4+ inches in diameter) cannot be ruled out with any persistent, longer-lived supercell; however, supercell longevity remains somewhat uncertain. Severe wind gusts and perhaps a brief tornado are also possible. While the exact timing of convective initiation is uncertain, a Severe Thunderstorm Watch will likely be needed within the next 1-2 hours to cover this potential. Some recent CAM solutions also indicate some potential for upscale growth later this evening; however, this scenario remains unclear. Should this occur, a transition towards damaging wind gusts as the primary threat could be expected

details.label: Discussion
details.text: Developing/agitated cumulus are noted underneath an upper-level cirrus canopy as of 1830 UTC via recent satellite imagery. Aided by weak forcing for ascent associated with a subtle mid-level perturbation progressing quickly eastward out of southern Ontario, continued insolation to the south of a weak surface cold front is expected to support isolated to widely scattered thunderstorm development over the next 1-3 hours. Effective shear of 30-35 kts and around 1000-1500 J/kg MLCAPE will promote some potential for a few stronger updrafts. Water-loaded downbursts capable of isolated damaging wind gusts will be possible with these more robust updrafts given modestly steep low-level lapse rates and a corridor of locally greater PW (1.5-1.75"). An instance of marginally severe hail also cannot be ruled out with any transient supercell structure that can develop. Weak mid-level lapse rates should largely temper overall convective intensity and severe coverage, however. Thus, watch issuance is not anticipated at this time
